questions.prompt: In an MLA 9 parenthetical citation, which form correctly cites page 12 of a work by Smith, Jones, and Lee when the author's name is not named in the sentence?
choices: (Smith and Jones 12)
(Smith, Jones, and Lee 12)
(Smith et al., 12)
(Smith et al. 12)
questions.explanation: For three or more authors, MLA 9 uses the first author's name followed by et al. and places the page number directly afterward.
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A journalism handbook says to use affect as a verb and effect as a noun. Which sentence follows the handbook?
choices: The new policy will effect every department and may have a significant effect on enrollment.
The new policy will effect every department and may have a significant affect on enrollment.
The new policy will affect every department and may have a significant affect on enrollment.
The new policy will affect every department and may have a significant effect on enrollment.
questions.explanation: Affect is the verb describing the policy's action, while effect is the noun naming the result it may have on enrollment.
questions.skill: Distinguishing affect from effect by grammatical function

questions.prompt: A student compares a model version listing the pen, notebook, and folder with a version listing the pen, notebook and folder. The guide requires a comma before the final conjunction in a series. Which comparison is accurate?
choices: The second version follows the guide, while the first omits its required comma.
Both versions follow the guide because the final comma is optional in every series.
The first version follows the guide, while the second omits its required comma.
Neither version follows the guide because series cannot contain conjunctions.
questions.explanation: Because the guide requires a comma before the final conjunction, the first version complies and the second does not.
questions.skill: Comparing a recorded model with a style guide
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use who for people and which for things, even when each modifies a singular noun. Which sentence complies with the guide?
choices: The coach which trained the team received an award.
The coach who trained the team received an award.
The player which won the match received a medal.
The bicycle who the coach repaired was stolen.
questions.explanation: The guide requires who for a person, and the relative pronoun who correctly refers to the coach.

questions.prompt: A school newspaper's style guide says to identify people by a neutral condition or diagnosis, not by a mobility device and not with phrases such as suffering from. Which sentence complies with the guide?
choices: A student with cerebral palsy presented the findings.
A student confined to a wheelchair presented the findings.
A student suffering from cerebral palsy presented the findings.
A wheelchair-bound student presented the findings.
questions.explanation: The phrase with cerebral palsy identifies the student neutrally by a condition without defining the person by a device or using a disparaging expression.

questions.prompt: A publication's style guide requires double quotation marks and places commas inside closing quotation marks when the comma belongs to the surrounding sentence. Which sentence complies?
choices: The editor said, ‘Submit the revision by Friday,’ and left.
The editor said, “Submit the revision by Friday,” and left.
The editor said, “Submit the revision by Friday”; and left.
The editor said, “Submit the revision by Friday”, and left.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses double quotation marks and places the comma inside the closing quotation mark, matching both rules.

questions.prompt: A hiking club's guide says farther refers to physical distance and further refers to an additional degree or extent. Which word correctly completes the sentence: The path continued ___ into the canyon than the old trail?
choices: far
further
farther
furthest
questions.explanation: Farther is the comparative adverb for physical distance, so it correctly describes how far the path continued into the canyon.
questions.skill: Applying a style guide's distinction between farther and further

questions.prompt: A publication's style guide says that a singular noun takes a singular verb even when a prepositional phrase follows it. Which sentence complies with the guide?
choices: Each of the articles need a final review.
The list of draft ideas need another round.
Each of the articles needs a final review.
Several editors has approved the draft.
questions.explanation: The singular subject Each takes the singular verb needs, even though the prepositional phrase of the articles separates them.

questions.prompt: According to AP style, which sentence correctly distinguishes a countable noun from an uncountable noun?
choices: The revised draft has fewer errors, but it has less ambiguities.
The revised draft has less errors, but it has fewer ambiguity.
The revised draft has fewer errors, but it has less ambiguity.
The revised draft has fewer errors, but it has fewer ambiguity.
questions.explanation: AP style uses fewer with countable nouns such as errors and less with uncountable nouns such as ambiguity.

questions.prompt: According to AP style, what is the status of singular they when referring to one person whose gender is unknown or irrelevant?
choices: Reject it in formal writing as grammatically incomplete.
Accept it when one person's gender is unknown or irrelevant.
Reserve it for groups of mixed-gender people.
Allow it only when a writer identifies the person's gender.
questions.explanation: AP style accepts singular they in formal writing when a person's gender is unknown or irrelevant to the sentence.

questions.prompt: A medical writing guide defines affect as a verb meaning influence and effect as a noun meaning a result. Which word correctly completes the sentence: The changed dosage may ___ the patient's response.
choices: affect
effect
affects
effecting
questions.explanation: Affect is the verb meaning influence, so it correctly expresses how the changed dosage may influence the patient's response.
questions.skill: Distinguishing the verb affect from the noun effect

questions.prompt: A communications guide requires introductory modifiers to attach clearly to the subject. Which sentence avoids a dangling or misleading modifier?
choices: After reviewing the draft, the manuscript was sent to the author.
After reviewing the draft, the editor sent it to the author.
Before approving the proposal, the schedule was moved to Friday.
By comparing the scores, the winner was announced.
questions.explanation: In the correct sentence, the editor is both the subject of sent and the understood agent of reviewing the draft.

questions.prompt: According to APA 7, how should the title of a book appear in a reference-list entry?
choices: Set the title in quotation marks.
Leave the title in plain text.
Set the title in bold.
Italicize the title.
questions.explanation: APA 7 italicizes the title of a book in a reference-list entry.

questions.prompt: A style guide requires the two parts introduced by not only and but also to use the same grammatical form. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The coach not only praised the team's effort but also questioning its tactics.
The coach not only praised the team's effort but also questioned its tactics.
The coach not only praise the team's effort but also questioned its tactics.
The coach only praised the team's effort but also questioned its tactics.
questions.explanation: The not only and but also clauses are parallel because both use the past-tense verbs praised and questioned.

questions.prompt: According to MLA 9, which sentence correctly uses a relative pronoun in a nonrestrictive clause?
choices: The trail, who followed the river, ended at the lake.
The trail, that followed the river, ended at the lake.
The trail, which followed the river, ended at the lake.
The trail, where followed the river, ended at the lake.
questions.explanation: In a nonrestrictive clause, MLA 9 uses which rather than that to mark the information as supplementary.
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A local style guide says to use a semicolon to join two independent clauses. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The road flooded; the storm overwhelmed the culvert.
The road flooded; because the storm overwhelmed the culvert.
Because the road flooded; the storm overwhelmed the culvert.
Although the road flooded; the storm overwhelmed the culvert.
questions.explanation: Both sides of the semicolon are independent clauses, so the sentence meets the guide's semicolon rule.
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide prohibits stacked negative constructions in formal prose. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: There aren't no errors in the report.
There is not no errors in the report.
There are not none errors in the report.
There are no errors in the report.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses the single negative word no rather than combining it with another negative expression.

questions.prompt: A nonprofit's style guide requires because, rather than since or as, to introduce a direct reason. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The workshop was delayed since the projector failed.
The workshop was delayed because the projector failed.
The workshop was delayed as the projector failed.
The workshop was delayed so the projector failed.
questions.explanation: Because introduces the direct reason that the projector failed, exactly as the style guide requires.
questions.skill: Choosing a conjunction for a direct reason under a style guide

questions.prompt: A school newspaper requires MLA for submitted features, but a contributing writer brings sentences formatted in AP. Which editorial approach best follows the style guide?
choices: Choose each convention according to the length of the sentence.
Keep the AP sentences because they are easier for readers to understand.
Use AP for quotations and MLA for the writer's own sentences.
Convert the sentences to MLA conventions and use MLA consistently throughout the feature.
questions.explanation: Using the required guide consistently, including within quotations, prevents mixed style conventions.

questions.prompt: According to APA 7, how are reference-list entries formatted with respect to indentation?
choices: Use a 0.5-inch block indent.
Use a 1-inch hanging indent.
Use a 0.5-inch hanging indent.
Use a 1-inch block indent.
questions.explanation: APA 7 reference-list entries use a 0.5-inch hanging indent, with the first line flush left.

questions.prompt: A journal's style guide says to use the objective-case pronoun whom after a preposition. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The reviewer to whom the editor sent the manuscript returned it promptly.
The reviewer who the editor sent the manuscript returned it promptly.
The reviewer which the editor sent the manuscript returned it promptly.
The reviewer to who the editor sent the manuscript returned it promptly.
questions.explanation: The objective-case pronoun whom correctly fills the object slot after the preposition to.

questions.prompt: A school publication's style guide says to introduce examples in formal prose with the words for example, followed by a comma. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: As an example, the survey found that most students preferred notebooks.
For example the survey found that most students preferred notebooks.
For instance, the survey found that most students preferred notebooks.
For example, the survey found that most students preferred notebooks.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses the guide's required introductory phrase and places a comma after it.
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: During a class debate, one group argues that a comma before a final conjunction is mandatory in every English sentence, while another cites a publication that omits it. Which summary accurately explains their disagreement?
choices: The groups are debating a disputed convention, and the publication can choose a house style without making that choice universal.
No style guide may prefer either convention when two connected items appear in a series.
The publication's house style proves that every sentence must omit the comma before its final conjunction.
The first group is correct because every English sentence requires a comma before its final conjunction.
questions.explanation: A style guide can establish a preferred convention for a publication without proving that the convention is required in every English sentence.
questions.skill: Distinguishing house style from universal usage rules
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: According to AP style, how much space should follow the period at the end of a sentence in typed text?
choices: Use one space.
Use two spaces.
Use no space.
Use a tab.
questions.explanation: AP style specifies one space between sentences in typed text.

questions.prompt: A magazine's style guide requires dates in day-month-year order with the month spelled out. Which date follows the guide?
choices: 14 March 2026
March 14 2026
March 14, 2026
questions.explanation: The date 14 March 2026 uses the required day-month-year order and spells out the month.

questions.prompt: A theatre's style guide treats the audience as a singular collective noun. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The audience stay seated silently until the lights came up.
The audience are seated silently until the lights came up.
The audience remain seated silently until the lights came up.
The audience is seated silently until the lights came up.
questions.explanation: Because the guide treats audience as a singular noun, the present-tense verb is correctly agrees with it.

questions.prompt: A student newspaper's style guide says to spell out numbers below 10 and use numerals for 10 and above in body text. Which sentence complies?
choices: We surveyed 12 students in two classes.
We surveyed twelve students in 2 classes.
We surveyed 12 students in 2 classes.
We surveyed twelve students in two classes.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses a numeral for 12 and spells out two, matching the guide's rule for body text.

questions.prompt: A research journal's style guide says to treat data as a plural noun. Which sentence complies with the guide?
choices: The collected datum show a clear pattern.
Each of the collected data show a clear pattern.
The collected data shows a clear pattern.
The collected data show a clear pattern.
questions.explanation: The plural noun data takes the plural verb show, matching the journal's stated usage rule.

questions.prompt: In an MLA 9 works-cited list, which author-name format is correct for a book by Jane Smith and John Doe?
choices: Jane Smith and John Doe.
Smith, Jane, and John Doe.
Smith, Jane, and Doe, John.
Doe, John, and Jane Smith.
questions.explanation: MLA 9 reverses only the first author's name and presents the second author's name in normal order.

questions.prompt: A school publication's guide requires who for people and which for things. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The teacher that led the workshop will grade the papers.
The teacher which led the workshop will grade the papers.
The teacher whom led the workshop will grade the papers.
The teacher who led the workshop will grade the papers.
questions.explanation: Who refers to the teacher and functions as the subject of led, matching the guide's required pronoun for people.
questions.skill: Selecting a relative pronoun according to a style guide

questions.prompt: A workshop guide says to use a colon after a complete introductory sentence when the following list completes the thought. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The workshop requires three items; a notebook, a pen, and a folder.
The workshop requires three items, including a notebook, a pen, and a folder.
The workshop requires: three items including a notebook, a pen, and a folder.
The workshop requires three items: a notebook, a pen, and a folder.
questions.explanation: The introductory clause before the colon is a complete sentence, and the list after it completes the thought.
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A research guide says to state an arithmetic difference between two percentages in percentage points and a relative change with percent. The response rate rose from 40% to 50%. Which sentence reports the change correctly?
choices: The response rate increased by 10 percent.
The response rate increased by 10 percentage points.
The response rate increased to 10 percentage points.
The response rate increased by 10 points.
questions.explanation: The difference between 50% and 40% is 10 percentage points, which describes the arithmetic change.

questions.prompt: According to APA 7, how should a standard abbreviation be introduced the first time it appears in a manuscript?
choices: Spell out the term, place the abbreviation in parentheses, and use the abbreviation afterward.
Use the abbreviation first, spell out the term afterward, and keep using the abbreviation.
Spell out the term each time it appears, and do not use the abbreviation afterward.
Use the abbreviation throughout, and explain it in a footnote on first mention.
questions.explanation: APA 7 introduces an abbreviation by spelling out the term first, placing the abbreviation in parentheses, and using the abbreviation in later mentions.
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A publishing guide requires a hyphen in a compound modifier placed before the noun it modifies. Which sentence applies the rule correctly?
choices: The editor sent a well written draft to the writer.
The editor sent a last minute revision to the writer.
The editor sent a last-minute revision to the writer.
The editor sent a loosely written draft to the writer.
questions.explanation: In the correct sentence, last-minute is hyphenated because it functions as a compound modifier immediately before revision.

questions.prompt: According to MLA 9, how should the protocol in a source's URL be handled in a Works Cited entry?
choices: Retain https:// at the start of the URL.
Replace https:// with www.
Omit https:// from the URL.
Change the URL to a DOI.
questions.explanation: MLA 9 generally presents URLs in Works Cited entries without the https:// or http:// protocol.

questions.prompt: A government agency's guide says the number of takes a singular verb. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The number of applications submitted by the deadline has risen sharply.
The number of applications submitted by the deadline have risen sharply.
The number of applications submitted by the deadline are rising sharply.
The number of applications submitted by the deadline rise sharply.
questions.explanation: The guide requires singular agreement with the number of, so has is the correct verb.

questions.prompt: A nonprofit's style guide says assure means to tell someone confidently. Which sentence uses assure in that sense?
choices: The counselor assured of the supplies' arrival.
The counselor ensured the volunteers that the supplies would arrive.
The counselor insured the volunteers against losses.
The counselor assured the volunteers that the supplies would arrive.
questions.explanation: In the correct sentence, assure means that the counselor told the volunteers confidently that the supplies would arrive.

questions.prompt: A school publication's guide says plural possessors take an apostrophe after the s, while singular possessors take 's. Which heading correctly labels essays written by several students?
choices: student's essays
students' essays
students essays'
students essays
questions.explanation: The plural possessive students' modifies essays and therefore takes an apostrophe after the s.

questions.prompt: In Chicago style title case, which word in the title 'The Art of War' is lowercased?
choices: of
Art
The
War
questions.explanation: Chicago lowercases short prepositions such as 'of' in title case.

questions.prompt: A style guide says that altogether means in total, while all together means collectively or at the same time. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The judges read twelve entries all together and then gathered the team all together.
The judges read twelve entries all together and then gathered the team altogether.
The judges read twelve entries altogether and then gathered the team all together.
The judges read twelve entries altogether and then gathered the team altogether.
questions.explanation: Altogether means in total, whereas all together means collectively or at the same time.

questions.prompt: Which style guide presents a notes-and-bibliography system for citing sources?

The Chicago Manual of Style
The AP Stylebook
The MLA Handbook
questions.explanation: The Chicago Manual of Style presents a notes-and-bibliography system in which numbered notes identify sources and a bibliography lists them.

questions.prompt: A laboratory's style guide requires instructions to use the simple present tense. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: Before each trial, mix the solution thoroughly.
Before each trial, mixed the solution thoroughly.
Before each trial, mixing the solution thoroughly.
Before each trial, have mixed the solution thoroughly.
questions.explanation: This sentence states the instruction with the simple present-tense verb mix.
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use double quotation marks for a complete quotation and single quotation marks for a quotation within it. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The editor said, 'Read the note labeled "Draft Two" before noon.'
The editor said, "Read the note labeled "Draft Two" before noon."
The editor said, "Read the note labeled 'Draft Two' before noon."
The editor said, "Read the note labeled Draft Two before noon."
questions.explanation: This sentence uses double quotation marks for the editor's words and single quotation marks for the nested label.
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A committee handbook says comprise is transitive, so it should not be followed by of, and the passive form is comprised is discouraged. Which sentence follows the handbook?
choices: The panel comprises of nine volunteer coaches.
The panel is comprised of nine volunteer coaches.
The panel comprises nine volunteer coaches.
The panel is comprising of nine volunteer coaches.
questions.explanation: Comprises directly takes nine volunteer coaches as its object and avoids both of and the discouraged passive construction.
questions.skill: Applying a style guide's rule for the verb comprise

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use an en dash with no spaces for a range of page numbers. Which citation follows the guide?
choices: See pages 10-12 for the full discussion.
See pages 10–12 for the full discussion.
See pages 10 – 12 for the full discussion.
See pages 10 to 12 for the full discussion.
questions.explanation: The option uses an en dash with no spaces between the two endpoints of the page range.
questions.topic: Record and Compare - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A publication's guide says a nonessential appositive that renames a noun should be enclosed by a pair of commas. Which sentence follows the guide?

Dr. Elena Ruiz, the school counselor led the session.
Dr. Elena Ruiz, the school counselor, led the session.
Dr. Elena Ruiz the school counselor, led the session.
questions.explanation: The appositive the school counselor is enclosed by a pair of commas because it renames Dr. Elena Ruiz.

questions.prompt: A magazine's style guide requires different from when comparing two things. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The revised proposal is different from the version discussed in May.
The revised proposal is different than the version discussed in May.
The revised proposal is different to the version discussed in May.
The revised proposal is different as the version discussed in May.
questions.explanation: Different from is the required comparison form, and the proposal is being compared with the earlier version.

questions.prompt: A style guide requires adjectives in this order: opinion, size, age, shape, color, origin, material, and purpose. Which phrase follows that order?
choices: a old small blue wooden chair
a small old blue wooden chair
a blue old small wooden chair
a small blue old wooden chair
questions.explanation: This phrase correctly orders the adjectives by size, age, color, and material.

questions.prompt: A travel publication's style guide says to omit the comma before the final conjunction in a simple three-item series. Which sentence follows the guide?

Tourists visited Paris, Rome and Athens.
Tourists visited Paris Rome and Athens.
Tourists visited Paris and Rome and Athens.
questions.explanation: The guide asks for no comma before the final conjunction, so the list with and but no comma before it complies.

The results were inconclusive — the sample was too small.
The results were inconclusive– the sample was too small.
The results were inconclusive—the sample was too small.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses an em dash with no spaces on either side.
